title: Chickwheat Shreds
subtitle: homemade shreddable seitan
menu_blurb: A homemade seitan of chickpeas, miso and vital wheat gluten, steamed until it pulls apart in tender, chicken-like shreds.
intro: What makes this unique is the texture: this seitan looks like chicken. Chickwheat has a meaty bite and a different mouthfeel from other kinds of seitan. Chickpeas, miso, onion, garlic, and vinegar balance the natural flavor of the gluten.
origin: Shreddable faux chicken has been around for a long time; Chinese and Taiwanese faux meat makers have been selling it for decades. Making it easily at home is newer. Shredded “chikun” was widely introduced by chef Skye Michael Conroy in his 2015 cookbook, Seitan and Beyond.

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A blender, a food processor, foil, and a steamer

steps.title: Blend
instructions: Blend everything except the vital wheat gluten in a high-speed blender until completely smooth, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Rest
instructions: Combine the chickpea mixture and the vital wheat gluten in a large bowl.
Let it rest for 15 minutes so the gluten absorbs the moisture.

steps.title: Knead in the food processor
instructions: Divide the dough in two. Process each half until warm and stretchy; it will come together into a large ball.
If it is too crumbly, add a few more tablespoons of liquid.

steps.title: Wrap and steam
instructions: Wrap each piece of dough in foil, folded into a rectangular package with the ends sealed tightly, then wrap in a second sheet of foil.

steps.title: Shred
instructions: Once cooled, shred gently along the grain.

tips.label: Kneading
tips.tip: The dough heats up as it processes. Let it cool a bit, then process again a few times until stretchy.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Mix in your own flavorings of choice.

nutrition.notes: Nutrient-dense legumes full of plant protein, fiber and minerals. They support heart and digestive health, keep you full, and help regulate blood sugar.
A good source of vitamin K, manganese, copper and zinc, with probiotics that support gut health. Made from soy, it is a complete protein.
A good source of iron, and one of the most protein-dense plant foods available.

notebook.question: What is seitan?
answer: Seitan is a popular plant-based meat substitute made entirely from gluten, the main protein found in wheat. Often called “wheat meat,” it is prized by vegans and vegetarians for its dense, chewy, stringy texture.

notebook.question: Is seitan healthy?
answer: It can be an excellent, protein-rich addition to a plant-based diet.

benefits.label: High in protein
benefits.text: A 2-ounce serving packs about 17 g of protein.

benefits.label: Low in calories and fat
benefits.text: It contains almost no fat and very few carbohydrates.

benefits.label: Nutrient dense
benefits.text: It provides good amounts of iron, selenium, and calcium.

benefits.label: Soy-free
benefits.text: A great plant-based protein for anyone with a soy allergy. It does contain gluten.
